section_summary: This section begins with SCAP research material on the charter, bylaws, leadership, organization, and senior personnel of the Broadcasting Corporation of Japan. It then documents occupation-era control of Japanese radio communications through SCAP directives, station-frequency amendments, police-radio lists, and State Department transmittals. The final portion contains March 1948 amendments to official lists of land, ship, and coastal radio stations, including call signs, frequencies, locations, vessels, and operating agencies.

subfiles.title: The Charter of the Broadcasting Corporation of Japan, with By-law
subfiles.from: Radio Research Unit, Research and Information Division, Civil Information and Education Section, GHQ SCAP
subfiles.about: Translation of the Broadcasting Corporation of Japan's charter and implementing bylaw as published on October 31, 1945.
subfiles.summary: The charter defines the corporation's broadcasting and radio-telecommunication purposes, legal style, Tokyo headquarters, membership, officers, governing boards, meetings, assets, accounts, and dissolution. Supplementary provisions regulate transitional terms and elections after the war. An annexed bylaw sets rules for budgets, borrowing, committees, directors' decisions, superintendents, and councillors.

subfiles.title: Broadcasting Corporation of Japan—Names and Brief Biographical Notes on Presidents and Appointed or Elected Officials
subfiles.from: Radio Research Unit, Research and Information Division, Civil Information and Education Section, GHQ SCAP
subfiles.about: Report on the presidents, official structure, staffing, and senior personnel of the Broadcasting Corporation of Japan.
subfiles.summary: The report lists the corporation's presidents since 1925 and provides biographical sketches of Kenzō Iwahara, Shichirō Komori, Hiroshi Shimomura, and Hachirō Ōhashi. It describes appointed and elected offices, staff totals, and senior personnel at central stations and administrative, program, and technical divisions. An appendix reports Ōhashi's February 20, 1946 resignation and names Kenjirō Yabe as the corporation's temporary external representative.

subfiles.title: Despatch No. 630: Control of Radio Communications in Japan
subfiles.from: United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: Transmits SCAPIN 1222 and its amendments to authorized frequencies and police-radio-station lists.
subfiles.summary: The despatch follows an earlier communication on control of Japanese radio communications. It forwards three copies of the September 20, 1946 SCAP directive, noting its frequency amendments and approval for retention, but not operation, of listed police radio stations.

subfiles.title: SCAPIN 1222: Control of Radio Communications
subfiles.from: General Headquarters, Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers
subfiles.to: Imperial Japanese Government, through the Central Liaison Office, Tokyo
subfiles.about: Approves amendments to Japanese radio-frequency assignments, extends the licensing deadline, and lists police radio stations approved for retention.
subfiles.summary: The memorandum approves changes proposed by the Ministry of Communications and distinguishes newly authorized stations from alterations to existing assignments. It approves retention of specified police radio stations without authorizing their operation, extends the licensing deadline to November 1, 1946, and clarifies transmitter-power limits. The enclosures provide extensive additions and deletions to frequency lists and a nationwide geographical list of Home Ministry police radio stations.

subfiles.title: Secretary of State Transmittal to the Federal Communications Commission
subfiles.about: Forwards a copy of the Political Adviser's despatch and SCAPIN 1222 on control of radio communications in Japan.
subfiles.summary: The Secretary of State encloses the October 3, 1946 despatch from the United States Political Adviser for Japan. The enclosure includes the September 20 SCAP directive and its frequency and police-station lists for the FCC's information.

subfiles.title: Receipt of Preliminary Report on Radio Broadcasting in Japan
subfiles.from: Frank A. Schuler, Jr., Chief, Japan and Korea Branch, Division of Occupied Areas
subfiles.about: Confirms receipt of the October 22, 1945 Preliminary Report on Radio Broadcasting in Japan.
subfiles.summary: This brief internal government memorandum records that the Japan and Korea Branch received the cited preliminary report. It supplies no substantive discussion of the report's findings.

subfiles.title: Despatch No. 70: Transmitting Lists of Japanese Radio Stations
subfiles.about: Transmits January 1, 1948 lists of Japanese land, ship, and coastal radio stations.
subfiles.summary: The despatch forwards three copies each of two lists prepared by the Radio Bureau of the Japanese Ministry of Communications. One covers Japanese radio stations generally and the other covers ship and coastal stations.

subfiles.title: Despatch No. 212: Control of Radio Communications
subfiles.from: United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: Transmits SCAPIN 1744/6 and bimonthly amendments to Japanese radio-station lists.
subfiles.summary: The despatch encloses five copies of the March 20, 1948 SCAP memorandum and its two enclosures. It explains that the attachments consolidate additions, deletions, and changes to the lists of Japanese land, ship, and coastal radio stations.

subfiles.title: SCAPIN 1744/6: Control of Radio Communications
subfiles.from: General Headquarters, Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers
subfiles.about: Reaffirms radio-station amendments authorized during January and February 1948 and introduces two revised station lists.
subfiles.summary: The memorandum refers to SCAPIN 1744 of July 14, 1947 and its subsequent amendments. It states that the attached bimonthly lists contain all additions, deletions, and changes to the land and maritime station lists. It also reaffirms amendments previously authorized through direct communications between SCAP's Civil Communications Section and the Ministry of Communications.

subfiles.title: Amendment to List of Japanese Radio Stations, Effective March 1, 1948
subfiles.about: Lists additions, deletions, and changes to Japanese land-radio stations, frequencies, and call signs.
subfiles.summary: The amendment supplies geographical entries for domestic, international, broadcast, police, railway, maritime, meteorological, aeronautical, lighthouse, and other stations. Each record may identify a SCAP registration number, frequency, call sign, power, emission class, operating limitations, station name, location, and coordinates. Separate sections revise the geographical emergency-police list and the frequency and call-sign indexes.

subfiles.title: Amendment to List of Japanese Ship and Coastal Radio Stations, Effective March 1, 1948
subfiles.about: Records additions, deletions, and changes to licensed Japanese ship and coastal radio stations.
subfiles.summary: The list is organized by radio region and prefecture and identifies vessels by SCAP registration number, name, port of registry, tonnage, operating agency, call sign, frequencies, power, and emission type. The additions include fishing vessels, merchant ships, government vessels, and meteorological craft throughout Japan. Later sections delete transferred or withdrawn registrations and amend the particulars of existing vessels; the changes list continues beyond page 80.
